summary: Characterized when the PyMuPDF fallback converter tier helps vs. hurts and corrected the falsified universal-remedy claim. Resolved the two candidate class-boundary framings (bibliography density vs. OCR vintage) into one mechanistic discriminator: Class A defects are introduced by the primary tier's own markdown-structuring heuristics (table misdetection, <sup>/<sub> span space-dropping) and are fixed by the fallback tier regardless of scan status (savage_1972, bacon_dorr_2024_classicism, Goldblatt/Hodkinson/Venema 2003); Class B defects are already baked into the source text layer (poor-vintage OCR) and no converter tier can fix them (joyce_1999, fallback makes it slightly worse). Confirmed scanned-vs-born-digital is not the discriminator using an independently-found corroborating case (bacon_dorr_2024_classicism, very likely born-digital) not supplied in the task description. Proposed exact replacement text for the falsified remedy sentence at literature_quality_gate.py:238-239 that preserves the untouched prohibition (lines 236-241) byte-for-byte for task 104 to narrow separately, and proposed a new 'Converter Tier Selection' section for context/guides/literature-organization.md plus a README cross-reference. Did not propose any auto-selection mechanism, per the task's explicit scope discipline.

memory_candidates.content: In the literature extension's converter pipeline (agent-system/extensions/literature/scripts/literature_quality_gate.py), 'scanned vs. born-digital' is NOT a reliable predictor of whether LITERATURE_CONVERTER=fallback fixes a gate rejection. The real discriminator is defect origin: defects introduced by the pymupdf4llm primary tier's own markdown-structuring heuristics (table misdetection over dense back matter, <sup>/<sub> footnote-span space-dropping) are fixed by the fallback tier regardless of scan status (proven on both a scanned book, savage_1972, and a born-digital paper, bacon_dorr_2024_classicism). Defects already baked into the source text layer (typically poor-vintage OCR) are untouched by either converter tier and can be slightly worsened by the fallback tier's own column-clustering noise (joyce_1999: 4 primary hits -> 5 fallback hits). Diagnose by inspecting where sentence_boundary_glue_count() hits fall (positionally concentrated near structural boundaries -> try fallback; scattered singly -> suspect OCR text-layer defect, needs re-OCR not a converter switch) rather than by document provenance.
